basics.name: Tommaso Mencattini
basics.label: MSc Data Science Student & Researcher
basics.summary: MSc student in Data Science at EPFL with research experience at ISTA, ETH Zürich, and GLADIA. My work focuses on large language models, interpretability, causal inference, and AI safety. First-author papers at ICLR, ICML, and ACL, plus publications at NeurIPS workshops and ECAI. Co-PI of a Coefficient Giving-funded research team on activation steering at Rome AI Safety.

work.name: Rome AI Safety (RAIS)
work.summary: Proposer and co-PI, together with Donato Crisostomi, of a 7-person research team funded by Coefficient Giving with $80k.
highlights: Developing disentangled, composable steering vectors for fine-grained behavioral control via white-box interventions in activation space.

work.name: Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)
work.summary: Research on causality and multimodal foundation models within the Locatello Group (PI: Francesco Locatello).
highlights: Co-first author of an ICLR 2026 Oral (top 1.2%): a framework (theory + library) for unsupervised causal effect discovery in RCTs.

work.name: GLADIA · Sapienza University of Rome
work.summary: Research on scalable model merging, interpretability, and ability estimation for large language models (PI: Emanuele Rodolà).
highlights: Scaled evolutionary model merging of LLMs to consumer GPUs and developed ability-estimation theory via Item Response Theory: 50× faster, 2% of the data, 85% performance retained. Two first-author papers at ICML 2025 and ACL 2025.
Co-first author of an ICLR 2026 paper proving injectivity of LLM hidden representations and presenting the first exact inversion algorithm (5M views on the tweeprint).

work.name: ETH Zürich (LRE Lab)
work.summary: Applied causal inference to explain and assess LLM performance on math word problems (PI: Mrinmaya Sachan).
highlights: Worked on applying causal inference techniques to large language models to detect spurious heuristics in reasoning tasks.
Ran large-scale experiments on high-performance computing clusters.

work.name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam · KAI Lab
work.summary: Mitigated hallucinations in LLMs using knowledge graphs for content planning (PI: Ilaria Tiddi).
highlights: Designed Text-to-Graph and Graph-to-Text methods for content planning.
Trained and evaluated multiple knowledge-graph-integrated LLMs.

work.name: Sapienza University of Rome
work.summary: NLP research in e-justice applications using specialized large language models.
highlights: Developed GPT-2-based writing assistant for legal documents.

work.name: Network Institute VU Amsterdam
work.summary: Technical support for interdisciplinary projects in XR, VR, and motion capture.
highlights: Worked with Unity, C#, iClone, Motive, and Optitrack.
Organized and presented at Surf XR-On Tour and Reshaping Work 2022 Conference.

courses: Coursework focused on the Mathematics of data science
Honours Programme (30 credits of advanced coursework, e.g. PDEs)
Studied sparse autoencoder diffing and transfer; work accepted at the UniReps Workshop @ NeurIPS 2024 (blog post track).
Focused on formal logic and philosophy of language
